interrupt latency is 12 * 20 = 240 bytes.
Alternative Verification: Minimum FIFO headroom = Rate_Bps * L_max = (96 * 10^6 / 8) * (20 * 10^-6) =

question:
An I/O receiver continuously ingests an external data stream at a constant rate of 96 Megabits/s (96 ×
106 bits/s = 12 bytes/μs) and asserts an interrupt when its internal hardware FIFO reaches the trigger
threshold. If the CPU's worst-case interrupt response latency from assertion until the ISR begins
draining the FIFO is Lmax = 20 μs, the minimum additional FIFO buffer capacity (in bytes) above the
threshold required to prevent receiver overrun during Lmax is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Because an MSI/MSI-X interrupt is a standard posted PCIe memory write to the
target core's APIC/GIC address, PCIe's Producer-Consumer ordering guarantees that all preceding DMA
payload writes from the device reach coherent memory before the MSI write triggers the CPU interrupt,
while supporting up to 2,048 distinct per-queue vectors in MSI-X (Option B).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing PCIe Base Specification (MSI/MSI-X and Posted Write ordering rules)
confirms Option B.
question:
Why did PCI Express (PCIe) replace legacy shared level-triggered interrupt pins (INTA#..INTD#)
with Message Signaled Interrupts (MSI / MSI-X)?
options: MSI/MSI-X requires 2,048 dedicated copper interrupt pins on the PCIe connector

MSI/MSI-X delivers an interrupt as an in-band posted memory-write transaction (`MemWr` of a
specific data payload to a special LAPIC/GIC doorbell physical address), eliminating dedicated
sideband interrupt wires, avoiding false-sharing ISR chains on shared `INTx` lines, and automatically
ordering the interrupt behind all prior DMA data writes on the same PCIe path
MSI/MSI-X forces the CPU to poll I/O ports every 10 ns
Legacy `INTx` pins can address up to 65,536 cores per device without any APIC

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Precise state requires committing all older instructions and squashing all younger
instructions (A, D is false); out-of-time pipeline exceptions must be ordered by program order at commit
(B); and asynchronous external interrupts differ from synchronous restartable faults (C) (A, B, C).
Alternative Verification: Verifying Smith & Pleszkun's precise interrupt architecture confirms A, B, and C.
question:
Which of the following statements regarding Precise Exceptions and External Interrupts in pipelined
and out-of-order processors is/are CORRECT?
options:
An exception at instruction `I_k` is **precise** iff all instructions preceding `I_k` in dynamic
program order (`I_0 .. I_{k-1}`) have completed and committed their architectural state updates, no
instruction after `I_k` (`I_{k+1} ..`) has modified architectural state, and `EPC` points cleanly to `I_k`
(or `I_k + 4` for traps)

When instruction `I_k` suffers an Instruction TLB/Page Fault during `IF` while an older instruction
`I_{k-1}` suffers a Data TLB/Page Fault during `MEM` in a 5-stage pipeline (`I_{k-1}`'s fault occurs in
a *later* clock cycle than `I_k`'s fault), hardware must record faults in pipeline latches and take `I_{k1}`'s exception first at the `MEM/WB` commit point

External I/O interrupts are asynchronous to the instruction stream and can be recognized
between any two instructions at the commit stage, whereas synchronous page faults or divide-byzero exceptions must be serviced at the exact faulting instruction `I_k` so `I_k` can be restarted

In a processor with precise exceptions, instructions after a page-faulting `LW` are allowed to
overwrite architectural registers permanently before the page fault handler runs

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:

misses. Each miss incurs 26 - 16 = 10 additional stall cycles due to DMA bus contention, totaling 1.2 * 10
= 12 million extra stall cycles.
Alternative Verification: Extra stalls = (60 * 20 / 1000) * (26 - 16) = 12 million cycles.
question:
A processor with an on-chip L1 cache executes a benchmark of 60 million instructions that incurs
MPKI = 20 L1 cache misses per 1,000 instructions. Because L1 hits do not access the external
system bus, cycle-stealing DMA transfers only delay the CPU when an L1 cache miss contends for the

cycles. Across the entire 60-million-instruction benchmark, the number of additional CPU stall cycles
(in millions of cycles) caused by DMA bus contention is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43

explanation:

Multiplying by the raw link bandwidth 20 GB/s gives 20 * 0.8 = 16 GB/s.

A multi-lane packetized I/O interconnect provides a post-encoding raw link bandwidth of 20 GB/s.
During a bulk DMA transfer, every Transaction Layer Packet (TLP) carries P = 128 bytes of DMA
payload data accompanied by H = 32 bytes of packet header, sequence number, and LCRC/ECRC
framing overhead (total packet size = 160 bytes). Assuming 100% link utilization by back-to-back
TLPs, the effective DMA payload throughput (in GB/s) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:

operation requires on average 0.60*(1) + 0.40*(4) = 2.2 physical disk I/Os. Thus maximum host IOPS =
2200 / 2.2 = 1000 IOPS.

question:
A RAID-5 storage array consists of N = 11 identical disks, each capable of sustaining 200 random
disk I/Os per second (IOPS). Under a small-block random workload with uniform load distribution
across all 11 disks, each host Random Read requires 1 physical disk I/O, whereas each host Small
Random Write incurs the RAID-5 Read-Modify-Write penalty of 4 physical disk I/Os (read old data,
read old parity, write new data, write new parity). For a mixed workload of 60% random reads and 40%
small random writes, the maximum sustainable aggregate host IOPS of the RAID-5 array is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Direct Cache Access (DCA / Intel DDIO) injects inbound DMA writes directly into the
CPU's shared Last-Level Cache (allocating/updating LLC lines) so that the network stack reads hot
packet headers/payloads at LLC latency without going to DRAM (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing Intel DDIO / Direct Cache Access architecture confirms Option A.
question:
In traditional DMA, an incoming network packet is written by the NIC to main memory (DRAM) while
invalidating any cached copy in the CPU's L3/L2/L1 caches, forcing the CPU to suffer a slow DRAM read
miss when it immediately inspects the packet header. How does Direct Cache Access (DCA / Intel
Data Direct I/O, DDIO) optimize high-speed I/O?
options:
The root complex routes incoming PCIe DMA writes from the NIC directly into a designated
portion (e.g., 2 ways) of the processor's shared Last-Level Cache (L3/LLC) rather than DRAM, and
serves outbound NIC DMA reads directly from the LLC, eliminating DRAM round-trips and cold cache
misses for active I/O buffers

DDIO disables the L3 cache and forces all CPU instructions to execute directly from the NIC's
EEPROM
DDIO requires the CPU to copy every packet byte-by-byte using Programmed I/O
DDIO only works on 110-baud RS-232 serial modems

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Common-clock buses are limited by flight time + skew (A); source-synchronous
strobes cancel flight delay across matched traces (B); and serial SerDes links embed the clock per lane
via CDR and line coding/scrambling (C); D is false (A, B, C).
Alternative Verification: Verifying high-speed I/O signaling principles confirms A, B, and C.
question:
Which of the following statements comparing Common-Clock Synchronous, Source-Synchronous,
and Embedded-Clock (SerDes / CDR) I/O interconnects is/are CORRECT?
options:
In a traditional **Common-Clock Synchronous Bus**, total bus flight time plus clock skew
between sender and receiver must be strictly less than one clock period (`t_flight + t_skew < T_clk`),
limiting the product of bus length and clock frequency

In a **Source-Synchronous Bus** (such as DDR SDRAM `DQS` data strobes), the transmitter
sends a clock/strobe signal alongside the data lines over matched-length PCB traces so that
common-mode flight delay cancels out, bounding the data rate by inter-trace skew rather than total
flight time

In high-speed serial interconnects (**PCIe, SATA, USB3**), a **Clock and Data Recovery (`CDR`)
PLL** extracts the symbol clock directly from transitions in each differential serial lane (guaranteed
by `8b/10b` or `128b/130b` scrambling), eliminating cross-lane clock-to-data skew altogether

Four-phase fully interlocked asynchronous handshaking is faster than a source-synchronous
burst over a 50-cm backplane

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: First, C_0 = 2^0 + 2^1 + 2^5 = 35. Second, for a constant initiation interval p to be
conflict-free across all future task pairs separated by k*p cycles (k >= 1), no multiple k*p may belong to
F = {1, 2, 6}. Testing p = 1, 2, ... shows the smallest integer with no multiple in F is p_const = 4. Thus C_0
+ p_const = 35 + 4 = 39.
Alternative Verification: State-transition check: advancing C_0 by p_const = 4 keeps bit c_4 = 0 at every
subsequent step, confirming p_const = 4 and C_0 + p_const = 39.
question:
A non-linear pipeline reservation table has forbidden latency set F = {1, 2, 6}. Let C0 = ∑f ∈ F 2f−1
be the decimal value of the initial collision vector (with c1 as LSB), and let pconst be the minimum
conflict-free constant initiation interval (i.e., the smallest integer p ≥ 1 such that a periodic schedule
initiating a new task every p cycles forever never collides, which requires k · p ∉ F for all integers k ≥
1). The sum C0 + pconst is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: I_1 (MUL) is in IF=1, ID=2, EX=3..8. With EX->EX forwarding: I_2 (ADD) executes EX in
cycle 9; I_3 (DIV) executes EX in cycles 10..23; and I_4 (ADD) executes EX in cycle 24, MEM in cycle 25,
and completes WB in cycle 26.
Alternative Verification: Total cycles = 2 (I_1 IF+ID) + 6 (I_1 EX) + 1 (I_2 EX) + 14 (I_3 EX) + 3 (I_4
EX+MEM+WB) = 26.
question:
A 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB, where IF, ID, MEM, WB each take 1 cycle and full EX
→ EX forwarding is supported) has three execution units in the EX stage: an integer ADD unit (1 EX
cycle), a multiplier MUL (6 EX cycles), and a divider DIV (14 EX cycles). Consider the 4-instruction
dependent sequence (with I1 fetched in cycle 1):
I1: MUL R1, R2, R3
I2: ADD R4, R1, R5
I3: DIV R6, R4, R7
I4: ADD R8, R6, R9
The clock cycle number in which instruction I4 completes its WB stage is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Resource MII: ResMII = max(ceil(6/2), ceil(7/2)) = max(3, 4) = 4. Recurrence MII:
RecMII = ceil(14/2) = 7. Thus 10 * ResMII + RecMII = 10 * 4 + 7 = 47.
Alternative Verification: Overall MII = max(4, 7) = 7, and 10*ResMII + RecMII = 47.
question:
A VLIW/superscalar compiler applies Modulo Scheduling (Software Pipelining) to an inner loop on a
processor with 2 integer ALU pipes and 2 Load/Store memory pipes (all fully pipelined, 1 initiation per
cycle per unit). Each loop iteration requires 6 ALU operations and 7 memory operations, and contains a
loop-carried recurrence cycle of total latency Lrec = 14 clock cycles across a dependence distance of
d = 2 iterations. Let ResMII = max(⌈6/2⌉, ⌈7/2⌉) be the Resource MII and RecMII = ⌈Lrec / d⌉ be
the Recurrence MII. The composite value 10 × ResMII + RecMII is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: In wave pipelining, multiple coherent wavefronts propagate concurrently through
combinational logic without intermediate latches, requiring tight balancing of minimum and maximum
path delays (t_max - t_min) to prevent wave collision (Option D).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing Cotton/Flynn wave-pipelining timing constraints confirms Option D.
question:
How does Wave Pipelining (Maximum-Rate Pipelining) differ from conventional synchronous
pipelining, and what timing parameter limits its maximum clock rate?
options: Wave Pipelining requires mechanical relays instead of CMOS transistors
Wave Pipelining works only when `t_max = 100 * t_min`
Wave Pipelining inserts 100 flip-flops per logic gate to slow down the signal

Wave Pipelining launches multiple successive data waves into a combinational logic block before
the first wave reaches the output *without* inserting intermediate pipeline registers; its clock period
is bounded below not by the maximum propagation delay `t_max` alone, but by the path-delay
variation `Delta_t = (t_max - t_min)` plus setup/hold/skew overheads so that a fast path of wave
`k+1` never overtakes a slow path of wave `k`

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: VLIW shifts scheduling and dependency checking to the compiler (A), stalls on
unpredictable dynamic cache misses better tolerated by OoO hardware (B), and uses template/stop bits
to avoid NOP padding (C), while strict VLIW exposes hardware latencies in the ISA (D is false) (A, B, C).
Alternative Verification: Comparing VLIW/EPIC (IA-64/TI C6x) and OoO Superscalar architectures
confirms A, B, and C.
question:
Which of the following statements comparing VLIW (Very Long Instruction Word) / EPIC architectures
against Out-of-Order Superscalar architectures is/are CORRECT?
options:
In a VLIW processor, the compiler statically packs multiple independent operations into a fixed
multi-operation bundle (e.g., 1 ALU + 1 MEM + 1 FP + 1 Branch), eliminating complex dynamic
hardware issue queues, dependency check matrices (`O(W^2)` comparators), and dynamic registerrenaming tables

When a loop has variable/unpredictable memory latencies (such as pointer-chasing cache misses)
or input-dependent memory aliasing, an Out-of-Order Superscalar processor can dynamically
schedule around the miss at runtime, whereas a purely static VLIW stalls the entire instruction bundle

Traditional VLIW code suffers from **NOP bloat (code expansion)** whenever an instruction
bundle has fewer independent operations than functional-unit slots, which compressed VLIW/EPIC
encodings mitigate using template/stop bits

VLIW binaries compiled for a 4-issue functional-unit configuration with specific pipeline latencies
are automatically binary-compatible with an 8-issue implementation that has different functional-unit
latencies without recompilation or translation

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: I_1 (DIV.D): Issue = 1, EX = 2..19, CDB = 20, Commit = 21. I_2 (ADD.D): Issue = 2, EX =
3..5, CDB = 6, and because the ROB commits in strict program order (1 instruction/cycle), I_2 commits in
cycle 21 + 1 = 22. Difference = 22 - 6 = 16 cycles.
Alternative Verification: Formula: L_div - L_add + 1 = 18 - 3 + 1 = 16 cycles.
question:
An out-of-order processor using Tomasulo's algorithm with a Reorder Buffer (ROB) issues 1
instruction per cycle in order and commits at most 1 instruction per cycle in order (`Issue` = 1 cycle,
`EX` = L cycles, `CDB Write-Result` = 1 cycle, `ROB Commit` = 1 cycle). Consider two adjacent
independent instructions:
I1: DIV.D F0, F2, F4 (EX latency Ldiv = 18 cycles; Issued in cycle 1)
I2: ADD.D F6, F8, F10 (EX latency Ladd = 3 cycles; Issued in cycle 2)
Instruction I2 completes its CDB Write-Result in cycle tCDB(I2) = 6, but must wait in the ROB until
I1 commits in cycle 21 before I2 can commit in cycle tCommit(I2) = 22. The number of clock cycles
tCommit(I2) − tCDB(I2) between I2's CDB broadcast and I2's in-order commit is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: When both predictors are wrong (30 branches), the tournament predictor always
mispredicts (30 mispredictions). When the two predictors disagree (150 branches), the meta-predictor
chooses the wrong predictor 10% of the time, adding 150 * 10% = 15 mispredictions. Total = 30 + 15 =
45 mispredictions per 1,000 branches.
Alternative Verification: Verify: 1000 * (0.03 + 0.15 * 0.10) = 45.
question:
A Tournament Branch Predictor combines a Local Predictor (PL) and a Global Predictor (PG) using a 2bit Meta-Predictor (Selector). Across a trace of 1,000 dynamic conditional branches:
• On 82% of branches (820 branches), both PL and PG predict correctly.
• On 3% of branches (30 branches), both PL and PG mispredict.
• On the remaining 15% of branches (150 branches), exactly one predictor is correct and the other is
wrong, and the Meta-Predictor selects the correct predictor 90% of the time.
The total number of branch mispredictions per 1,000 branches made by the Tournament Predictor is
__________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Unscheduled scalar loop takes 80 * 10 = 800 cycles. The 4x unrolled and scheduled
loop executes 80 / 4 = 20 unrolled iterations of 14 cycles each = 280 cycles. Total clock cycles saved =
800 - 280 = 520.
Alternative Verification: Per 4 elements, unrolling + scheduling reduces cycles from 4 * 10 = 40 to 14
(saving 26 cycles per 4 elements); across 20 groups of 4 elements, savings = 20 * 26 = 520 cycles.
question:
A scalar vector-scaling loop (LD, MUL.D, SD, ADDI, BNE — 5 instructions per element) executes
on an in-order pipelined processor. In the unscheduled scalar loop, each iteration incurs 2 Load-toMUL.D stall cycle(s), 2 MUL.D-to-SD stall cycles, and 1 branch stall cycle (5 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 10
clock cycles per element). When the compiler unrolls the loop 4 times (4 LDs, 4 MUL.Ds, 4 SDs, 1
ADDI, 1 BNE = 14 instructions per 4 elements) and schedules instructions to eliminate all pipeline
stalls (14 cycles per 4 elements), the total number of clock cycles saved across an array of N = 80
elements is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Speculative load bypassing hides unresolved store-address latency when
addresses do not alias, uses the Load Queue (LQ) to snoop later resolving store addresses for memoryorder violations, and uses Store-Set predictors (Chrysos & Emer) to delay only loads that historically
collided with an unresolved store (Option C).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing Out-of-Order Load/Store Queue (LSQ) memory disambiguation and
Store Sets confirms Option C.
question:
In an out-of-order processor, a younger Load instruction has already computed its effective address
EAload while an older Store instruction in the Store Queue (SQ) has not yet computed its effective
address EAstore. What is the trade-off of Speculative Load Bypassing (Memory Dependence
Prediction)?
options:
An older Store always forwards its data to all younger Loads even when their addresses differ by
1 MB
Memory disambiguation applies only to branch instructions

If the processor speculatively issues the younger `Load` to the L1 cache before `EA_store` is
known, most loads succeed early because `EA_load != EA_store`; however, if `EA_store` later
resolves to the same address (`EA_store == EA_load`), the Load Queue (`LQ`) detects a **MemoryOrder Violation** and must squash/replay the `Load` and its dependent instructions (which a
**Store-Set Predictor** prevents on repeat offending PCs)
Younger loads are never allowed to execute until all older stores are written to magnetic tape

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 43
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: ROB rollback restores architectural state (registers/memory) while leaving
microarchitectural cache state observable to timing attacks unless mitigated (A, B, C; D is false).
Alternative Verification: Verifying transient execution microarchitecture and Spectre/Meltdown
mitigations confirms A, B, and C.
question:
Which of the following statements regarding Transient / Speculative Execution, Precise Commit, and
microarchitectural cache side channels is/are CORRECT?
options:
When an out-of-order processor speculatively executes instructions along a mispredicted branch
path (or past a faulting load before retirement), the **Reorder Buffer (`ROB`)** squashes all
speculative **architectural** register/memory updates, but side effects on **microarchitectural**
state (such as which L1 data cache lines were brought into the cache) can persist unless explicitly
fenced or isolated

In **Branch Target Injection / Bounds-Check Bypass (`Spectre`)**, transient instructions along a
mispredicted branch perform an out-of-bounds array load `secret = A[x]` followed by a dependent
load `probe[secret * 4096]`, encoding the value of `secret` into the cache set occupancy of `probe`

Inserting a speculation barrier (`LFENCE` / `CSDB`) or index masking (`x = x & mask`) prevents
speculative loads from accessing unauthorized array offsets along transient paths

Squashing a mispredicted branch in the Reorder Buffer automatically resets all DRAM capacitors
in main memory to zero

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: 3-register instructions leave 2^4 - 13 = 3 prefixes -> 3*16 - 44 = 4 two-reg prefixes
-> 4*16 - 59 = 5 one-reg prefixes -> 5*16 = 80 zero-operand instructions.
Alternative Verification: Verify total encodings: 13*16^3 + 44*16^2 + 59*16 + 80 = 65536 = 2^16.
question:
A processor with 16-bit instructions and 16 general-purpose registers (4 bits per register field) uses an
expanding opcode scheme to encode 13 three-register instructions, 44 two-register instructions, and
59 one-register instructions. The maximum number of zero-operand instructions that can also be
encoded in the remaining bit space is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: In Little-Endian byte ordering, the 16-bit halfword at address 0x2003 places
M[0x2003] = 0x1E in the least significant byte (bits 7..0) and M[0x2004] = 0x0B in the most significant
byte (bits 15..8), forming 0x0B1E = 11*256 + 30 = 2846.
Alternative Verification: Converting 0x0B1E to decimal gives 2846.
question:
In a byte-addressable Little-Endian processor, four consecutive memory bytes starting at address
0x2002 contain:
M[0x2002] = 0xAA,   M[0x2003] = 0x1E,   M[0x2004] = 0x0B,   M[0x2005] = 0xFF
If the processor executes an unaligned 16-bit unsigned halfword load LHU R1, 0x2003, the unsigned
decimal value loaded into R1 is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Fixing the sign bit at inst[31] and maximizing bit-position overlap across I/S/B/U/J
formats reduces multiplexer fan-in and critical-path delay in the immediate generator (Option B).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing the RISC-V Unprivileged ISA Specification Section 2.3 (Immediate
Encoding Variants) confirms Option B.
question:
In the RISC-V 32-bit base integer ISA (RV32I), why are the immediate bits in conditional branch (Btype) and unconditional jump (J-type) instructions scrambled across the instruction word rather than
stored in contiguous bit order, while keeping the sign bit fixed at bit inst[31]?
options: Scrambling the immediate bits encrypts the machine code against hardware reverse engineering

Keeping the sign bit at `inst[31]` in every immediate format allows sign-extension to begin
immediately in the Decode stage in parallel with opcode decoding, and aligning each immediate bit
with its position in `I`-type/`S`-type formats minimizes the fan-in of the immediate-generation
multiplexers
RISC-V branches shift the immediate right by 4 bits before adding to the PC
B-type and J-type instructions do not use two's complement signed offsets

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Sign-extending 0xCC gives -52. Thus EA = R_base + R_idx * 4 + disp = 6000 + 20 *
4 + (-52) = 6080 - 52 = 6028.
Alternative Verification: Direct computation: 6000 + 80 - 52 = 6028.
question:
A processor evaluates a scaled-indexed with 8-bit signed displacement operand disp8(Rbase, Ridx,
4) where Rbase = 6000, Ridx = 20, scale factor = 4, and the 8-bit two's-complement displacement
byte is 0xCC (-5210). The resulting decimal Effective Address (EA) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: After fetching the 7-byte instruction at 5100, the sequential next-instruction PC is
5100 + 7 = 5107. Adding the signed displacement -37 yields Target = 5107 + (-37) = 5070.
Alternative Verification: Target = PC_start + L_inst + disp = 5100 + 7 + (-37) = 5070.
question:
A variable-length PC-relative branch instruction begins at memory byte address 5100. The instruction
consists of 5 bytes of prefix and opcode followed by a 2-byte signed displacement field containing -37
(total instruction length = 7 bytes). When the branch is taken, the decimal branch target address
loaded into the PC is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: In Register Indirect mode, the pointer is already in register R2 (1 memory read:
M[R2]), whereas in Memory Indirect mode @(A), the CPU must first read the pointer from M[A] and then
dereference M[M[A]] (2 memory reads) (Option C).
Alternative Verification: Comparing effective-address computation cycles confirms 1 vs 2 data-memory
accesses (Option C).
question:
For a single-operand load instruction LOAD R1, operand (assuming the instruction word has already
been fetched into the IR), how many data-memory read accesses are required in Register Indirect
addressing ((R2)) versus Memory Indirect (Deferred) addressing (@(A))?
options:
Register Indirect requires 2 data-memory reads and Memory Indirect requires 1 data-memory
read
Both modes require 3 data-memory reads after instruction fetch

Register Indirect `(R2)` requires 1 data-memory read (using `R2` directly as the effective
address), whereas Memory Indirect `@(A)` requires 2 sequential data-memory reads (1 to fetch the
pointer at `M[A]` and 1 to fetch the operand at `M[M[A]]`)
Both Register Indirect and Memory Indirect require 0 data-memory reads

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: In 8-bit two's complement arithmetic, (50 - 125) mod 256 = (-75) + 256 = 181
(0xB5).
Alternative Verification: Using R1 + (255 - R2) + 1 = 50 + 130 + 1 = 181 with carry-out C_out = 0.
question:
An 8-bit ALU executes the subtraction R1 ← R1 − R2 (implemented as R1 + ~R2 + 1) with initial
values R1 = 50 and R2 = 125. If the resulting 8-bit binary pattern stored in R1 is interpreted as an
unsigned 8-bit integer (0..255), its decimal value is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Rotating 11100101_2 left by 3 positions shifts the low 5 bits left by 3 and wraps the
top 3 bits into the LSBs, yielding 00101111_2 = 0x2F = 47.
Alternative Verification: ((0xE5 << 3) & 0xFF) | (0xE5 >> 5) = 47.
question:
An 8-bit register initially holds R = 0xE5 (111001012). After executing a circular Rotate Left (ROL)
by 3 bit positions (without carry), the unsigned decimal value stored in R is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Each contiguous block of 1s in Radix-2 Booth recoding generates exactly 2 active
operations (1 subtraction at the LSB of the run and 1 addition at the bit position immediately above the
MSB of the run). For 3 disjoint runs, Booth performs 2 * 3 = 6 add/sub operations, saving 12 - 6 = 6
operations.
Alternative Verification: Savings = N_ones - 2 * K_runs = 12 - 6 = 6.
question:
A 16-bit positive two's-complement multiplier (b15 = 0) contains a total of 12 ones arranged into 3
disjoint contiguous runs (blocks) of ones (each run having length ≥ 3). Compared to a naive unsigned
shift-and-add multiplier that performs one addition per 1-bit (12 additions), the number of
add/subtract operations saved by Radix-2 Booth's algorithm is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: A 3:2 CSA tree compresses N vectors down to 2 vectors (Sum S and Carry C) in
O(log_{3/2}(N)) full-adder delays, after which a final Carry-Propagate Adder merges S + C into a single
binary representation (Option C).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing Wallace/Dadda multiplier architecture confirms Option C.
question:
In a high-speed hardware multiplier using a Wallace Tree or Dadda Tree of Carry-Save Adders (3:2
compressors) to sum N partial products, why is a conventional Carry-Propagate Adder (CPA, such as
a Carry-Lookahead Adder) still required at the final stage?
options: The final Carry-Propagate Adder is used only to compute the parity bit of the multiplier
Carry-Save Adders can only add 1-bit numbers

Each 3:2 CSA stage reduces three input vectors to two output vectors (a redundant Sum vector
`S` and shifted Carry vector `C`) without propagating carries horizontally; once the tree reduces all
`N` partial products down to a final pair `(S, C)`, a Carry-Propagate Adder is needed to add `S + C`
into a single non-redundant binary product

A 3:2 CSA reduces three operands directly into one final binary number in a single full-adder
delay

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: The AND-plane has P * 2I = 28 * 22 = 616 crosspoints, and the OR-plane has P * O
= 28 * 24 = 672 crosspoints. Total = 28 * (22 + 24) = 1288.
Alternative Verification: Direct formula: P * (2*I + O) = 28 * 46 = 1288.
question:
A hardwired control unit is synthesized as a Programmable Logic Array (PLA) with I = 11 input
variables (each available in both true and complemented form in the AND-plane, i.e., 2I = 22 literal
lines), P = 28 shared product-term lines, and O = 24 control-signal output OR-lines. The total number
of programmable crosspoints (links) in the combined AND-plane and OR-plane (P × (2I + O)) is
__________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Average cycles = (1 - 0.80) * 3 + 0.80 * 5 = 0.60 + 4.00 = 4.6.
Alternative Verification: Using c_nt + p_taken * (c_t - c_nt) = 3 + 0.80 * 2 = 4.6.
question:
In a non-pipelined multi-cycle processor with a sequence-counter control unit, a conditional branch
instruction BEQ requires 3 clock cycles when Not-Taken (asserting SC_CLR early) and 5 clock cycles
when Taken (to compute and load the branch target into PC). If 80% of executed BEQ instructions are
Taken, the average number of clock cycles per BEQ instruction is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Synchronizing asynchronous inputs into a single clean synchronous signal prevents
metastability and incoherent multi-bit state transitions across the FSM's state register (Option D).
Alternative Verification: Digital control unit design rules confirm the necessity of input synchronization
for asynchronous external status lines (Option D).
question:
Why must an asynchronous external input signal (such as an I/O IRQ or memory READY/WAIT line)
be passed through a two-flip-flop synchronizer before feeding the next-state combinational logic of a
multi-flip-flop Hardwired Control Unit?
options: Asynchronous signals are always stuck at logic 0

Synchronous binary counters cannot be clocked without a two-flip-flop synchronizer on their
clock pin
A two-flip-flop synchronizer increases the clock frequency of the control unit by 2x

If an asynchronous signal transitions near the active clock edge and fans out directly to multiple
state flip-flops, different path delays or setup/hold violations can cause some state flip-flops to see
`0` while others see `1` (or enter metastability), transitioning the FSM into an illegal/corrupted state

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Each microinstruction is 64 / 8 = 8 bytes. For 4096 = 4K microinstructions, total
capacity = 4 * 8 = 32 KB.
Alternative Verification: Total bits = 262144; dividing by (8 * 1024) = 8192 bits/KB yields 32 KB.
question:
A microprogrammed control unit has a Control Store of 4096 microinstructions, where each
microinstruction is 64 bits wide. The total storage capacity of the Control Store in Kilobytes (KB,
where 1 KB = 1024 bytes) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: A 6-bit CD field provides 2^6 = 64 encodings. Subtracting the 2 reserved encodings
(Always-0 and Always-1) leaves 62 encodings. Since each status flag uses 2 encodings (true and
complement), the maximum number of distinct status flags is (62) / 2 = 31.
Alternative Verification: Formula: 2^(6 - 1) - 1 = 32 - 1 = 31.
question:
In a microprogrammed control unit, a 6-bit condition-select field (CD) drives a 26:1 condition
multiplexer. Two encodings of CD are reserved for Unconditional Branch (1) and Sequential Increment /
No Branch (0), while the remaining 26 − 2 encodings are paired so that each architectural/datapath
status flag Fi can be tested in both true (Fi = 1) and complemented (Fi = 0) polarities. The
maximum number of distinct status flags Fi that can be supported is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: The pipelined microcycle clock period is T_u = max(14, 16) + 1 = 17 ns. Executing N
= 11 sequential microinstructions through a 2-stage pipeline takes N + 1 = 12 microcycles = 12 * 17 =
204 ns.
Alternative Verification: Verify: (11 + 1) * 17 = 204 ns.
question:
A microprogrammed control unit pipelines microinstruction fetch and datapath execution across two
stages (Stage 1: Control Store access tCS = 14 ns; Stage 2: Datapath execution tDP = 16 ns)
separated by a Microinstruction Register (MIR) with latch overhead treg = 1 ns. The microcycle clock
period is Tμ = max(tCS, tDP) + treg. To execute a branch-free micro-routine of N = 11
microinstructions through this 2-stage micro-pipeline (N + 1 microcycles including fill), the total time
required (in ns) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Pipelining Control Store fetch (Stage 1) with datapath ALU execution (Stage 2)
means that a conditional micro-branch depending on Stage-2 flags cannot steer the Stage-1 address
mux until the end of the cycle, creating a 1-microcycle branch delay slot (Option D).
Alternative Verification: Analyzing pipelined microprogrammed control hazards confirms Option D.
question:
When a microprogrammed control unit uses a Microinstruction Register (MIR) to overlap the fetch of
microinstruction Ik+1 from the Control Store with the datapath execution of microinstruction Ik, what
happens when Ik is a conditional micro-branch that depends on an ALU status flag generated at the
end of Ik's execution cycle?
options: The ALU status flags are computed 3 cycles before `I_k` enters the `MIR`
Overlapping Control Store fetch with datapath execution eliminates all conditional micro-branches
The Control Store predicts 100% of ALU flags before the instruction is fetched from main memory

Because the branch condition from `I_k`'s ALU operation is not valid until the end of `I_k`'s
datapath cycle, the Control Store has already fetched the sequential microinstruction `I_{k+1}` during
that cycle, creating a 1-microcycle micro-branch delay slot (which must either be squashed as a NOP
bubble on a taken branch or filled with an independent microinstruction)

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: A 512 KB = 512 * 1024 = 2^19 byte region uses the lower 19 address lines
(A_18..A_0) for internal byte addressing. Full decoding without aliasing requires decoding all remaining
32 - 19 = 13 upper address lines (A_31..A_19).
Alternative Verification: 32 - log2(512 * 1024) = 32 - 19 = 13 address lines.
question:
In a processor with a 32-bit byte-addressable physical address bus (A31..A0), an SRAM region of
size 512 KB (1 KB = 1024 bytes) is mapped using full (exhaustive) address decoding with zero
aliasing. Since the lower address lines select bytes within the 512 KB region, the number of upper
address lines that must be fed into the region's Chip-Select (CS) address comparator/decoder is
__________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Let h be the row-buffer hit rate. Then 10*h + 50*(1 - h) = 22 => 40*h = 28 => h = 28 /
40 = 70%.
Alternative Verification: Check: 0.70 * 10 + 0.30 * 50 = 22 ns.
question:
An SDRAM controller using an open-page policy services a Row-Buffer Hit in Thit = 10 ns (tCL only)
and a Row-Buffer Conflict (Miss) in Tmiss = 50 ns (tRP + tRCD + tCL). To achieve an average DRAM
access latency of 22 ns, the required Row-Buffer Hit Rate (in %) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: XORing the low bank bits W[2:0] with the next higher address slice W[5:3] ensures
that both unit-stride (where W[2:0] cycles 0..7) and stride-8 (where W[5:3] cycles 0..7) distribute
across all 8 banks with zero conflicts (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Verifying B = W[2:0] ^ W[5:3] for W = 8*i (i=0..7) confirms B = 0 ^ i = i (all 8
banks visited cleanly, Option A).
question:
In an 8-way low-order interleaved memory where bank index is simply B = W mod 8 (the lowest 3
word-address bits), accessing an array with stride S = 8 routes every single access to Bank 0 (1/8
bandwidth). How does XOR-based bank permutation (B = W[2:0] ⊕ W[5:3]) resolve this bank
conflict for stride-8 accesses?
options:
As the word address advances by stride 8 (`W = 0, 8, 16, 24, ...`), bits `W[2:0]` remain constant
(`000`) while bits `W[5:3]` increment through `000, 001, 010, ..., 111`, so `B = W[2:0] ^ W[5:3]`
cycles conflict-free through all 8 banks (`0, 1, 2, ..., 7`)
XOR permutation increases the physical DRAM refresh interval from 64 ms to 64 seconds
XOR permutation converts DRAM cells into 6-transistor SRAM latches
XOR permutation forces all stride-1 accesses to collide in Bank 0

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: The per-way cache size is 256 KB / 8 = 32 KB, whereas the unmapped page offset
covers only 16 KB. Thus log2(32 / 16) = 1 index bits come from the VPN, creating 2^1 = (32 KB) / (16 KB)
= 2 possible synonym cache sets per physical block.
Alternative Verification: Number of synonym sets = Way_Size / Page_Size = (256 / 8) / 16 = 2.
question:
A processor uses a Virtually Indexed, Physically Tagged (VIPT) L1 cache of total capacity 256 KB
organized as a 8-way set-associative cache, while the virtual memory page size is 16 KB. Because the
per-way size (32 KB) exceeds the 16 KB page size, several upper index bits come from the Virtual
Page Number (VPN). If two different virtual pages are mapped to the same physical frame without OS
page coloring, the maximum number of distinct cache sets (synonym locations) in which the same
physical block could potentially reside is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Sector offset bits = log2(256) = 8 bits; sector index bits = log2(1024) = 10 bits.
Shared Tag per sector = 40 - 10 - 8 = 22 bits. Adding 4 * (1 Valid + 1 Dirty) = 8 sub-block status bits
gives 22 + 8 = 30 metadata bits per sector.
Alternative Verification: Tag (22 bits) + 4 * 2 status bits (8 bits) = 30 bits.
question:
A direct-mapped Sector (Sub-block) Write-Back Cache uses a 40-bit byte-addressable physical
address and contains 1024 sectors. Each sector holds 4 sub-blocks of 64 bytes each (total sector
data size = 256 bytes). Each sector stores one shared Tag field, while each individual sub-block has
its own 1-bit Valid flag and 1-bit Dirty flag. The total number of metadata bits per sector (Tag + all
sub-block Valid/Dirty bits) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: In 0-indexed row-major layout, A[8][15] is element index 8 * 20 + 15 = 175, at byte
offset 175 * 4 = 700 bytes from Base. Dividing by the 32-byte block size gives block number floor(700 /
32) = 21, which maps to Set (21) mod 128 = 21.
Alternative Verification: Set = floor(((r * C + c) * elem_size) / B) mod N_sets = floor(700 / 32) mod 128 =
21.
question:
A cache has 128 sets (indexed 0 to 127) and a cache block size of 32 bytes. A 2D array A[0..31]
[0..19] of 4-byte elements is stored in row-major order starting at an aligned base address that maps
to Set 0, byte offset 0. The decimal cache set index to which element A[8][15] maps is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Way prediction speculatively activates a single way in the first cycle (achieving
direct-mapped speed and power on a correct way prediction) and checks the other ways in an extra
cycle only on a way misprediction (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Analyzing L1 cache way-prediction microarchitecture confirms Option A.
question:
In an L1 data cache, Phased (Serial) Tag-First Access reads and compares all K tags before enabling
only the single matching data SRAM way (saving dynamic power at the cost of higher hit latency). How
does Way Prediction achieve both single-way dynamic power savings and fast single-cycle parallel
access latency on most hits?
options:
Way Prediction uses a small predictor table to pre-select and read only ONE predicted data way
(and its tag) in Cycle 1; on a way-prediction hit (~85–90% of L1 hits), data is delivered in 1 cycle with
1/K data-array power, while a way-misprediction falls back in Cycle 2 to check the remaining K-1 ways
Way Prediction disables all tag comparators so that tag mismatches are never checked
Way Prediction writes every store to all K ways in the set simultaneously
Way Prediction converts a set-associative cache into a magnetic disk

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: The initial miss stalls the CPU for 24 cycles until the critical word arrives. The
remaining 7 words take 7 cycles to fill the line. Since the CPU executes 2 useful cycles during this
background fill before issuing the next Load, that Load stalls for the remaining (7 - 2) = 5 cycles. Total
stall cycles = 24 + 5 = 29.
Alternative Verification: Equivalently, full-line transfer time is 24 + 7 = 31 cycles, of which 2 cycles are
overlapped with useful CPU execution, leaving 31 - 2 = 29 stall cycles.
question:
A single-ported L1 cache with 8-word blocks uses Critical-Word-First with Early Restart. On a cache
miss, the critical word arrives from memory after 24 clock cycles (allowing the CPU to resume
immediately), while the remaining 7 words of the block continue streaming into the cache at 1 word per
cycle (occupying the cache port for the next 7 cycles). If the CPU executes 2 non-memory cycles after
resuming and then issues another Load that must wait for the ongoing line fill to finish, the total
number of CPU stall cycles caused by this miss (initial critical-word wait + secondary line-fill port
contention) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Effective miss penalty = (50% * 1) + (50% * 25) = 13 cycles. Thus AMAT = 1 + 0.12 *
13 = 2.56 cycles.
Alternative Verification: Verify: 1 + 0.06*1 + 0.06*25 = 2.56.
question:
A direct-mapped L1 cache has a hit time of 1 clock cycle and a miss rate of 12%. An off-L1 miss to main
memory incurs a penalty of 25 clock cycles. Adding a small fully-associative Victim Cache intercepts
50% of all L1 misses and services them with a penalty of only 1 extra clock cycle(s) (while the
remaining 50% of L1 misses miss in the Victim Cache and incur the 25-cycle memory penalty). The
resulting Average Memory Access Time (AMAT) (in clock cycles) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Starting from 011_2, hitting Way 3 updates its path bits, and hitting Way 1 updates
its path bits, yielding final state (100)_2 = 4.
Alternative Verification: Tracing each tree bit update confirms (100)_2 = 4.
question:
A 4-way set-associative cache uses a 3-bit Tree Pseudo-LRU (tPLRU) state (b0b1b2)2 per set,
where b0 is the root bit (0 → left subtree Ways {0,1}; 1 → right subtree Ways {2,3}), b1 is the leftsubtree bit (0 → Way 0; 1 → Way 1), and b2 is the right-subtree bit (0 → Way 2; 1 → Way 3). On each
hit, the bits along the accessed path are flipped to point away from the accessed way. Starting from
state (b0b1b2)2 = 0112, after a hit to Way 3 followed by a hit to Way 1, the resulting decimal value of
the 3-bit state (b0b1b2)2 (0..7) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Standard Write-Allocate must perform a Read-For-Ownership (RFO) line fill on the
first sub-line store because only 1 word is written initially; instructions like ARM DC ZVA / x86
MOVNTDQ or per-word valid bits (Write-Validate) avoid the wasted RFO read (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Analyzing Read-For-Ownership (RFO) overhead in streaming writes confirms
Option A.
question:
When a program executes a memset(buf, 0, N) loop that sequentially writes every 4-byte word of a
large cold buffer (64-byte cache lines, 16 words per line) without ever reading buf beforehand, why
does a naïve Write-Back + Write-Allocate cache still perform one unnecessary 64-byte memory read
per cache line unless hardware supports Write-Validate / Cache-Line Zero (DC ZVA / CLZERO)?
options:
Because the first 4-byte store to a cold 64-byte line only modifies 4 of the 64 bytes, a standard
Write-Allocate cache cannot know that the remaining 60 bytes will also be overwritten later, so it
fetches the old 64-byte line from DRAM (Read-For-Ownership) before merging the first 4-byte store
Write-Back caches never allocate lines on store misses

Fetching the old 64-byte line from DRAM is required to compute the parity of the CPU instruction
pointer
A 64-byte cache line can only hold 1 byte of data

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Entry address = IVT_Base + V * Entry_Size = 4096 + 54 * 8 = 4096 + 432 = 4528.
Alternative Verification: Direct calculation confirms 4096 + 432 = 4528.
question:
A processor's Interrupt Descriptor / Vector Table (IDT / IVT) base register points to byte address
4096, and each interrupt descriptor entry occupies 8 bytes. When an I/O controller signals vectored
interrupt number V = 54, the decimal memory byte address from which the CPU fetches descriptor V
is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Available interrupt cycles per second = 600 * 10^6 * 0.15 = 90,000,000 cycles/s.
Dividing by 1500 cycles/interrupt gives 60,000 interrupts/s = 60 kIRQ/s.
Alternative Verification: (600 * 1000 * 0.15) / 1500 = 60 kIRQ/s.
question:
A processor running at 600 MHz (600 × 106 cycles/s) requires 1500 clock cycles to service each I/O
interrupt (including context save, ISR body, and return). If interrupt servicing is budgeted to consume at
most 15% of total CPU clock cycles, the maximum sustainable interrupt rate (in thousands of
interrupts per second, kIRQ/s) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Interrupt coalescing batches multiple DMA completion events using a count
threshold and bounded latency timer so that context-switch and ISR overhead is amortized across
many packets (Option B).
Alternative Verification: Analyzing high-speed NIC/NVMe interrupt moderation and NAPI polling
confirms Option B.
question:
At 100 Gbps network line rates (where millions of packets arrive per second), raising a separate
hardware interrupt for every single packet causes receive livelock (the CPU spends 100% of its time in
interrupt entry/exit). How does hardware Interrupt Coalescing (Interrupt Moderation) solve this
problem?
options: Interrupt Coalescing drops 99% of incoming network packets in hardware

The controller buffers multiple completed packet descriptors in DMA ring memory and uses a
packet-count threshold (`N` packets) and an expiration timer (`T` microseconds) to raise a single
hardware interrupt that lets the OS harvest a batch of packets in one ISR/NAPI poll
Interrupt Coalescing slows the CPU clock down to match the Ethernet symbol rate
Interrupt Coalescing disables DMA and forces the CPU to read every byte using `IN` instructions

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Payload bursts = (48 * 1024) / 64 = 768. Descriptor bursts = (20 * 64) / 64 = 20.
Total memory bus bursts = 768 + 20 = 788.
Alternative Verification: Total bytes transferred over memory bus = 50432 bytes; dividing by 64
bytes/burst gives 788 bursts.
question:
A Scatter-Gather DMA controller transfers a total payload of 48 KB (1 KB = 1024 bytes) split across
20 non-contiguous memory buffers. For each buffer fragment, the DMA controller fetches one 64-byte
Scatter-Gather Descriptor from main memory before transferring the fragment payload. If every
memory bus burst transfers 64 bytes, the total number of memory bus bursts required for both
descriptor fetches and payload transfers is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: The IOMMU sits between I/O bus masters and main memory, translating deviceissued IOVAs to host physical addresses and enforcing per-device memory isolation and DMA
remapping (Option D).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing IOMMU DMA remapping and protection architecture confirms Option
D.
question:
Why is a hardware I/O Memory Management Unit (IOMMU, such as Intel VT-d or ARM SMMU)
essential when assigning a PCIe DMA device directly to an untrusted virtual machine or user-space
driver (e.g., VFIO / DPDK)?
options: DMA controllers cannot access RAM even when no IOMMU is present
An IOMMU replaces the CPU's Arithmetic Logic Unit during floating-point instructions
An IOMMU converts PCIe serial lanes into RS-232 UART ports

Without an IOMMU, a DMA controller issues physical memory addresses directly onto the memory
bus and could read or overwrite arbitrary host kernel or other VMs' physical frames; the IOMMU
translates I/O Virtual Addresses (`IOVA`) via device-specific page tables and blocks unauthorized
DMA accesses

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Expanding T_inst(k) = (T_comb/k + t_L)*(1 + alpha*k) = T_comb/k + (T_comb*alpha
+ t_L) + (alpha*t_L)*k. Setting d(T_inst)/dk = -T_comb/k^2 + alpha*t_L = 0 yields k* = sqrt(T_comb /
(alpha * t_L)) = sqrt(2025 / (0.6 * 15)) = sqrt(225) = 15 stages.
Alternative Verification: By AM-GM inequality, T_comb/k + (alpha*t_L)*k is minimized when T_comb/k =
(alpha*t_L)*k => k = sqrt(2025 / 9) = 15.
question:
An unpipelined processor has total combinational logic delay Tcomb = 2025 ps. When partitioned into
k uniform pipeline stages with latch overhead tL = 15 ps per stage, the clock period is Tclk(k) =
Tcomb / k + tL, while pipeline hazard penalties cause the average CPI to grow as CPI(k) = 1 +
0.6k. Treating k as a continuous variable, the optimal number of pipeline stages k* that minimizes the
average time per instruction Tinst(k) = Tclk(k) × CPI(k) is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Setting bit c_f = 1 (weight 2^(f-1)) for each forbidden latency f in {2, 3, 6} gives C_0
= 2^1 + 2^2 + 2^5 = 38 (100110_2).
Alternative Verification: Binary representation (100110)_2 evaluates to 38 in base 10.
question:
A non-linear pipeline reservation table has maximum forbidden latency m = 6 and forbidden latency
set F = {2, 3, 6}. Using the standard collision vector convention C0 = (c6...c2c1)2 where ci = 1 iff i
∈ F (with c1 as the least significant bit, weight 20), the unsigned decimal value of the initial collision
vector C0 is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Superpipelining exploits temporal parallelism via finer stage subdivision (higher
clock rate, higher cycle-count latencies), while superscalar execution exploits spatial parallelism by
issuing multiple instructions per cycle across parallel functional units (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Comparing MIPS R4000 (superpipelined) vs Alpha 21164 / Intel Pentium Pro
(superscalar) confirms Option A.
question:
How does a Superpipelined processor (IPC ≤ 1, deep narrow pipeline with very high clock frequency)
fundamentally differ from a Superscalar processor (IPC > 1, multiple parallel execution pipelines at a
moderate clock frequency) in how it exploits Instruction-Level Parallelism (ILP)?
options:
A Superpipelined processor subdivides pipeline stages to increase clock frequency (issuing 1
instruction per short sub-cycle, which increases branch/load-use latency measured in clock cycles),
whereas a Superscalar processor duplicates fetch/decode/execution hardware to issue multiple
independent instructions in the same clock cycle

A Superpipelined processor executes 8 instructions in a single clock cycle without using any
pipeline registers
A Superscalar processor cannot execute more than 1 instruction every 10 clock cycles
Both architectures require source programs to be written in microcode

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Each branch incurs on average (60% * 1 control bubble) + (20% * 1 RAW stall) = 0.80
extra cycles. Across 15% branches, effective CPI = 1.0 + 0.15 * 0.80 = 1.12.
Alternative Verification: Control stalls/instr = 0.09; ID RAW stalls/instr = 0.03; Total CPI = 1.12.
question:
In a 5-stage RISC pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) that resolves conditional branches in the ID stage
(using a dedicated comparator in ID with EX → ID forwarding), every Taken branch incurs 1 controlflush bubble, and any branch that has an immediate RAW data dependency on the immediately
preceding ALU instruction incurs 1 data-hazard stall cycle before ID. In a program with ideal base CPI
= 1.0 (no other stalls), 15% of all instructions are conditional branches, 60% of conditional branches
are Taken, and 20% of conditional branches depend on the immediately preceding ALU instruction. The
effective CPI of the processor is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: On the 1st invocation, both predictors mispredict only the loop exit (1 misprediction).
On each of the remaining R - 1 = 24 invocations, the 1-bit predictor mispredicts BOTH the first
iteration's re-entry (predicting N after exit) and the loop exit (2 mispredictions/invocation -> 1 + 2*24 =
49 total), whereas the 2-bit counter drops only from 11 (ST) to 10 (WT) on exit and still predicts T on reentry (1 misprediction/invocation -> 25 total). Difference = 49 - 25 = 24.
Alternative Verification: Each of the 24 loop re-entries saves 1 misprediction with a 2-bit counter, giving
25 - 1 = 24 fewer mispredictions.
question:
An inner loop executes 8 iterations per invocation (7 Taken backward branches followed by 1 NotTaken loop-exit branch: T7N), and this inner loop is invoked R = 25 times in succession by an outer
loop. Assuming both predictors start in their Strong/Taken state (1 for the 1-bit predictor, 11 [Strongly
Taken] for the 2-bit saturating counter), how many fewer branch mispredictions does the 2-bit
saturating counter incur across all 25 invocations compared to the 1-bit predictor?

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: The 32 architectural registers always hold 32 committed physical registers, and the
120 in-flight ROB entries hold 80% * 120 = 96 speculative destination physical registers. Total allocated
physical registers = 32 + 96 = 128.
Alternative Verification: PRF_used = R_arch + N_inflight_dest = 32 + 96 = 128.
question:
An out-of-order superscalar processor with a unified Physical Register File (PRF) implements 32
architectural registers and a 120-entry Reorder Buffer (ROB). A physical register mapped to an
architectural register cannot be returned to the free list until the younger instruction that overwrites
that architectural register commits from the head of the ROB. In a workload where 80% of all in-flight
ROB instructions allocate a new destination register, the number of allocated physical registers when
the 120-entry ROB is completely full is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: A procedure called from multiple sites returns to a different caller address each time
from the same RET instruction PC; a LIFO Return Address Stack tracks the dynamic call chain
accurately (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Analyzing indirect jump prediction for procedure returns confirms Option A.
question:
Modern branch predictors use a dedicated hardware Return Address Stack (RAS) (pushing PC + 4 on
CALL and popping the predicted target on RET) rather than a standard Branch Target Buffer (BTB) to
predict function return addresses. Why does a single shared BTB entry fail to predict RET accurately
when a function foo() is called from many different call sites?
options:
Because `foo()` ends with a single `RET` instruction at a fixed PC, a standard BTB indexed by
that `RET`'s PC remembers only the most recent caller's return address and mispredicts every time
`foo()` is called from a different call site, whereas a LIFO hardware RAS matches the dynamic callstack nesting of `CALL` and `RET`
A standard BTB cannot store instruction addresses above 0x1000
The `RET` instruction always jumps to address 0x00000000
A hardware RAS can only predict forward conditional branches

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: With 15-bit instructions and 5-bit addresses: 25 two-address instructions leave 2^5
- 25 = 7 prefixes (7 * 2^5 = 224 one-address slots). Since 320 zero-address instructions consume 320 /
2^5 = 10 one-address slots, K = 224 - 10 = 214.
Alternative Verification: Conservation of encodings: 25*2^10 + K*2^5 + 320 = 2^15 => K = 214.
question:
A computer uses 15-bit instructions and 5-bit address fields. Using an expanding opcode scheme that
partitions the entire 215 encoding space with zero unused bit patterns, the ISA encodes exactly 25
two-address instructions, K one-address instructions, and 320 zero-address instructions. The exact
value of K is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Breaking 0x443A0000 into (S | E | M): S = 0, E = 136 (unbiased exponent e = 136 -
127 = 9), and 1.M * 2^9 = 744.
Alternative Verification: Direct bit-field decoding of 0x443A0000 confirms +(1.45312) * 2^9 = 744.
question:
A 32-bit word in memory contains the hexadecimal bit pattern 0x443A0000. When interpreted as an
IEEE-754 single-precision floating-point number (1 sign bit, 8-bit biased exponent with bias 127, and
23-bit fractional mantissa), its exact decimal value is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Each 16-bit compressed instruction saves 2 bytes compared to a 4-byte RV32I
instruction. Across 75% of 64,000 = 48,000 compressed instructions, total code bytes saved = 96,000
bytes. Dividing by 64 bytes/block saves 96,000 / 64 = 1500 instruction cache blocks.
Alternative Verification: Pure 32-bit blocks = (64000 * 4) / 64 = 4000; RV32IC blocks = 2500;
Difference = 1500.
question:
A sequential basic-block trace of 64,000 instructions executes on a RISC-V processor supporting the
16-bit compressed extension (RV32IC), where 75% of the instructions are encoded as 16-bit (2-byte)
compressed instructions and the remaining 25% are 32-bit (4-byte) instructions. Given a 64-byte
instruction cache block size, how many fewer 64-byte instruction blocks are fetched across this trace
compared to pure 32-bit RV32I encoding?

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Stack machines use implicit TOS operands (A is true, D is false); Accumulator
machines bottleneck on the single ACC register (B is true); and 3-address GPR Load-Store ISAs
facilitate compiler register allocation and ILP scheduling (C is true) (A, B, C).
Alternative Verification: Evaluating classical ISA taxonomy (Hennessy & Patterson Chapter 1 / Appendix
A) confirms A, B, and C.
question:
Which of the following statements comparing 0-Address (Stack), 1-Address (Accumulator), 2/3Address Register-Memory, and 3-Address Load-Store (GPR) instruction set architectures is/are
CORRECT?
options:
In a 0-address Stack machine, arithmetic instructions (`ADD`, `MUL`) pop their source operands
from and push their result to the top of the operand stack implicitly, achieving high static code
density for expression trees but creating a sequential bottleneck at the top-of-stack (`TOS`) register

In a 1-address Accumulator machine, every binary arithmetic operation implicitly uses the single
Accumulator (`ACC`) as both one source operand and the destination, forcing frequent memory
spills/reloads of intermediate subexpressions

A 3-address Load-Store architecture with 32 general-purpose registers enables graph-coloring
compiler register allocation and non-destructive register-to-register instruction scheduling (`R1 != R2,
R3`)
A 0-address Stack machine requires 4 explicit 5-bit register fields inside every `ADD` instruction

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: In 0-indexed Row-Major layout for A[D1][D2][D3], the linear element index of A[1][5]
[7] is ((1 * 12 + 5) * 10 + 7) = (17 * 10 + 7) = 177. Multiplying by 4 bytes/element and adding Base = 3000
gives 3000 + 708 = 3708.
Alternative Verification: EA = 3000 + 1*480 + 5*40 + 7*4 = 3708.
question:
A 0-indexed 3D array A[0..7][0..11][0..9] of 4-byte elements is stored contiguously in Row-Major
Order starting at memory byte address 3000. To access element A[1][5][7], the compiler generates
an indexed effective address calculation whose resulting decimal byte address is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: After f1's prologue, SP = 6000 - 96 = 5904. After f2's prologue, SP = 5904 - 48 =
5856. Saving RA at offset +40(SP) stores RA at byte address 5856 + 40 = 5896.
Alternative Verification: Verify: 6000 - 96 - 48 + 40 = 5896.
question:
In a RISC processor with a downward-growing stack, the stack pointer is initially SP = 6000 before
calling f1(). Function f1() executes prologue ADDI SP, SP, −96 and calls f2() via JAL RA, f2
(which writes the return address into register RA without modifying SP). Function f2() then executes

which f2()'s return address RA is saved is __________.

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:

question:

+ 8k, with 4-byte val at offset +0 and 4-byte next_idx at offset +4):

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:
Primary Derivation: Auto-increment loads require two register-file writes per load and complicate
precise exception rollback when a page fault occurs in MEM, whereas unrolled displacement offsets
achieve nearly identical dynamic instruction counts with simpler hardware (Option A).
Alternative Verification: Reviewing Hennessy & Patterson and Waterman's RISC-V design rationale
confirms Option A.
question:
Unlike ARMv7 or PDP-11, the RISC-V base integer ISA (RV32I / RV64I) omits dedicated AutoIncrement / Post-Indexed load/store instructions (LW Rd, (Rs1)+) and provides only Base-plus-12bit-Signed-Displacement (imm12(Rs1)) for data memory accesses. What is the primary
microarchitectural reason for omitting auto-increment loads in a pipelined RISC design?
options:
An auto-increment load writes TWO destination registers (`Rd` from memory at WB and `Rs1 <-
Rs1 + 4` from the ALU), which either requires a second register-file write port on every load or
creates structural/exception-recovery hazards if the load page-faults in MEM after `Rs1` was already
modified; in a loop unrolled `k` times, `imm12(Rs1)` accesses `0(Rs1), 4(Rs1), ..., 4(k-1)(Rs1)` with
only a single `ADDI Rs1, Rs1, 4k` per unrolled iteration
RISC-V processors cannot add constants to registers
Auto-increment addressing requires a 256-bit instruction word
Base-plus-displacement addressing cannot access array elements

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:

arbitrary ASLR base addresses (A), exploits the fixed link-time offset between .text and .got (B), and
resolves external symbols via GOT indirection (C); D is false (A, B, C).

question:
Which of the following statements regarding Position-Independent Code (PIC), Global Offset Tables
(GOT), and PC-Relative Addressing in shared libraries (.so / .dll) is/are CORRECT?
options:
Using PC-relative addressing for intra-module branches and data accesses allows the read-only
`.text` code segment of a shared library to be mapped at different virtual base addresses across
multiple processes while sharing the exact same physical RAM pages without text relocations

When a PIC shared library references an external global variable whose address is resolved by
the dynamic loader at load time, the code loads the variable's runtime pointer from an entry in the
`.got` and then dereferences that pointer

Position-Independent Code requires recompiling the shared library from C source code every
time a process calls `fork()`

paper: Computer Organization and Architecture Test Series — Test 44
subject: Computer Organization
explanation:

48 + 22 = 118 ps.
